### 1. Establishment and Management of the Institute Fund
- **Sources of Funds:** The Fund comprises all moneys received by or on behalf of the Institute from the Central Government; grants, gifts, donations, benefactions, bequests, or transfers; interests and profits arising from transactions involving Institute money; proceeds from the sale of journals, pamphlets, and books; and any other moneys received from any source. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
- **Deposit & Investment:** All moneys credited to the Fund shall be deposited or invested in a manner decided by the Institute, subject to the approval of the State Government. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
- **Application of Funds:** The Fund shall be applied towards meeting the expenses of the Institute, including costs incurred in the exercise of its powers and discharge of its functions under the Act. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]

### 2. Budgetary Provisions
- **Preparation & Submission:** The Director is mandated to prepare and lay the budget estimate for the next financial year before the Board on or before August 10 each year. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
- **Approval & Forwarding:** The Board must examine and approve the estimate (with or without modifications) by September 1 and forthwith submit a copy to the State Government. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
- **In-Year Modifications & Transfer Limits:** During the financial year, the Board may reduce any budget grant item or transfer amounts to other items. However, it cannot transfer non-recurring grants for recurring expenditure. Furthermore, the Board lacks the power to transfer from one item to another an amount exceeding 20% of the original grant under any given item. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]

### 3. Power of the Board Regarding Rules and Regulations
- **Statutory Rule-Making:** The rules framed under Section 16 of the Act are specifically noted to not provide for Provident Fund, Gratuity, or pension benefits. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
- **Board's Jurisdiction & Autonomy:** The Board functions as an independent juristic entity empowered to prepare its own budget. While State officers may be members of the Board, this composition does not render the Institute an extension of the State Government or a "State" under Article 12 of the Constitution. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
- **Audit Requirement:** The accounts of the Institute are required to be audited in accordance with statutory provisions. [Case: THE STATE OF BIHAR vs DR. SACHINDRA NARAYAN | No Citation | Supreme Court of India, 2019]
